_comment: Copy to config.json and edit for your project. This is the PUBLIC example with placeholder subject + reusable query groups (seeded from the thread-sweep themes). The real config.json is gitignored. Discovery is automated; posting is always a human gate (see the module README).

roles-architecture: system prompt per agent role duplication
dead-mans-switch: cron claude stopped running no error
credential-discipline: agent api keys env files leaked
agent-autonomy: should I automate this agent task
when to let an agent run autonomously
human in the loop vs full automation agent

reddit._caveat: DISCOVERY-ONLY and opt-in. Governed by the Reddit Data API terms; best-effort public JSON read for discovery only. NEVER automate posting. Reddit shadowban removals are INVISIBLE, so a posted-ledger entry for Reddit can be a lie — verify out-of-band before trusting it. Leave enabled=false unless you understand this.

stackexchange._caveat: DISCOVERY-ONLY and opt-in. Thin adapter (see ROADMAP.md: a dedicated stack-sweep module isn't worth building, this catches the residual long tail). The anonymous IP quota is small (roughly 300 requests/day, shared across every site queried) and a response can carry a `backoff` field demanding N seconds before the next request — this lane honours it automatically. Separately and just as load-bearing: Stack Overflow's own policy PROHIBITS AI-generated answer content, so this lane is discovery recall only — any reply a human chooses to write there must be genuinely human-authored and compliant with that policy. Leave enabled=false unless you understand both.

devto._caveat: DISCOVERY-ONLY and opt-in, the same gate as every other lane in this module. dev.to comment etiquette parallels the rest of the set: a reply must stand alone, and drive-by link-drops burn the account. Leave enabled=false unless you understand this.
